value.rationale: A natural operational question in a recently published two-stage GHZ protection protocol is whether an arbitrary number of intermediate local flips prevents finite-time loss of genuine multipartite entanglement. The theorem converts finite-size numerical strategy tables into an exact all-n formula, a unique critical initial damping budget, a sharp exponential n/m asymptotic, and concrete n=5 strategy distinctions. The complement-pair classification and strict global monotonicity are nontrivial structural statements rather than a fixed-size table recomputation; no claim about fidelity or actual device robustness is made.
